content.title: About
content.content: Toasted barley bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from whole barley kernels that are first toasted to a golden hue. It has a distinctive nutty aroma, a crisp crust, and a soft, slightly dense crumb. The bread is commonly used as a base for sandwiches, snacks, and soup accompaniments.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for more than 10,000 years.
Toasting the grain enhances its flavor and increases antioxidant levels.
Barley bread is often considered more nutritious than wheat bread because of its higher fiber and beta‑glucan content.
In several cultures, toasted barley bread is traditionally served with fish and seafood dishes.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Barley provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health and promoting satiety.

items.title: Lowers cholesterol
items.content: Beta‑glucans in barley can help reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Supports blood sugar control
items.content: The low glycemic index of barley bread helps stabilize post‑meal glucose spikes.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Barley supplies magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The product contains gluten and is unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Portions should be moderated for those following strict low‑carb diets.

items.title: Barley allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible allergic reactions to barley may occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted barley bread can be enjoyed as a snack, used for sandwiches and toast, served alongside soups and salads, or crumbled as a topping for casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a cool, dry place in an airtight bag or container. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent drying out and mold growth.
